title: Knowledge check: Creating and Using Components

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Creating and Using Components”?
options: Props flow down from parent to child; children emit events to request parent-owned state changes.
Child components should mutate props freely.
Slots can only contain plain text.
Every component should keep a private copy of all props.
questions.answer_key: Props flow down from parent to child; children emit events to request parent-owned state changes.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Creating and Using Components directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Defining an SFC component”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use Vue CLI as the primary new-project scaffolder without checking its status.
Edit generated dist assets as the source of truth.
Expose private credentials in client-side environment variables.
Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.answer_key: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Defining an SFC component”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Creating and Using Components” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
